# SyberLabs

> SyberLabs builds AI software that proves its work: SyberWork, an autonomous software factory; Attest, which proves every step your docs promise; RISE; and FLYSPACE. Custom AI consulting and design partnerships.

> **RISE and AI models:** since RISE #294 the RISE server calls no model. An AI reading request runs on the reader’s own connection: hosted Jev through the reader’s OpenRouter account, or a pinned Kev-4B on the reader’s machine (`/kev/` on the site). local Kev did not meet RISE’s bar in internal checks on RISE’s evaluations (RISE `docs/product/tasks/SCR-004.json`), and there is no production Kev deployment, by design. Once the reader connects, RISE’s visual direction sends sections of the reading text to that connection.

This file is generated from the site’s own data (projects/site-data.js in github.com/SyberLabs/SyberLabs.github.io) by scripts/llms.mjs. Each project line carries a "Reflects" stamp: the repository commit and date its claims were checked against. Every project claim is taken from its repository at the commit named in `reflects`, its public page, or docs/SYSTEM_MAPS.md. Evidence states follow MasterMind's discipline: implemented (the behaviour exists in code), tested (a named test exercises it), measured (numbers exist under stated conditions), deployed (it runs somewhere people can reach). Nothing is promoted from one state to the next by wording.

## When to use this file

- Use it to learn what SyberLabs is, which projects exist, what state each one has reached, and where its page, source and live app are.
- Use the "Reflects" commit as the version to read: for code-level questions, read the source repository at that commit (for example with a code index such as GitHits, where the repository is public).
- Quote the evidence lines as written. A project that is implemented or tested is not thereby deployed or measured, and "not yet" lines are part of the claim.
- Read the [full text](https://syberlabs.io/llms-full.txt) for every field each project page shows, including demo captions and run output.

## When not to use this file

- Do not treat it as newer than the Reflects stamp. If a repository has moved on, the repository is the authority for code and this file for what the site claims.
- Do not infer capabilities, users, metrics or deployments that are not stated here; the site states its limits on purpose.
- It describes a website. It is not an API, SDK or package, and it carries no credentials. Never send keys or private data to the contact address.

## Projects

- [SyberWork](https://syberlabs.io/projects/syberwork/): Autonomous software factory. The factory floor for AI agents that write, test and repair code. Every change is checked before it lands. Rules define the allowed steps, a named person approves the work, and a tamper-evident history records what was proposed, checked, approved and done.
  - Status: Work in progress
  - Reflects: SyberLabs/SyberWork@208eaf6 · verified 2026-10-05
  - Source: https://github.com/SyberLabs/SyberWork
  - Evidence, tested: Twenty-three golden conformance traces, a clean-install release gate and CI green on CPython 3.11 to 3.13.
  - Evidence, measured: On the author’s machine with the default SQLite sync: explain.allowed median 3.8 µs, complete_case median 37.4 ms, chain verification of 501 events median 10.2 ms.
  - Evidence, implemented: The included procurement case runs end to end against a separate reference system, with a real order POST under an idempotency key and manager sign-off.
  - Evidence, not yet: The service binds to loopback and has no deployment beyond one machine. No outside project consumes the SDK. The model-versus-patch benchmark has not been run against a real model.
- [Attest](https://syberlabs.io/projects/attest/): Document and spec verification. Point Attest at a README, a quickstart, an AI assistant’s how-to answer or a product spec. It runs every step against the real app, in a real browser, and hands the document back with each step marked proven, stale, broken, unverifiable or skipped, with evidence behind every mark.
  - Status: Open source · early
  - Reflects: SyberLabs/attest@274b8e7 · verified 2026-11-05
  - Source: https://github.com/SyberLabs/attest
  - Evidence, measured: At Kane CLI Hack Day in San Francisco on 24 October 2026, Attest proved 9 documents across 23 turns, with 31 browser claims proven by Kane, each with a screenshot.
  - Evidence, measured: Real drift it caught that day: Vite’s starter page now reads “Get started”, not “Vite + React”, and GitHub’s “Security & analysis” is now “Advanced Security”.
  - Evidence, tested: Unit tests and red-team cases cover forged approvals, attempts to weaken a protected promise and path-escape attacks on the apply step.
  - Evidence, not yet: There is no hosted service; Attest runs locally as a command-line tool. Shell steps run on the host, not in a sandbox. No outside team runs it in production yet.
- [RISE](https://syberlabs.io/projects/rise/): Interactive reading app. An interactive reading app that combines text, sound and moving visuals in your browser. Read words at a pace you choose, or switch to a page view.
  - Status: Live · open beta
  - Reflects: SyberLabs/RISE@998d725 · verified 2026-10-05
  - Source: https://github.com/SyberLabs/RISE
  - Live: https://rise.syberlabs.io/ (No account, no key and no install. Pick a reading and press Begin.)
  - Evidence, deployed: The reader, Library, Chapel, Make rooms and the interactive sample run at rise.syberlabs.io.
  - Evidence, tested: Unit, integration and browser suites run in CI; the first-load budget and the design diagram are checked on every release.
  - Evidence, measured: Composer in ChatGPT: a controlled developer-mode session on 2026-10-04 produced an admitted Current and narration the reader confirmed hearing. That is partial acceptance on one release, not a public listing.
  - Evidence, tested: RISE Plus voice, an optional ElevenLabs voice ($8.99 a month): implementation merged; paid launch pending verification. It runs in production on Stripe test mode: on 2026-10-08 a test purchase unlocked it and the voice was heard reading the buyer's own file.
  - Evidence, not yet: No reader study has been run; release evidence still records zero real-device and stranger-testing records.
- [FLYSPACE](https://syberlabs.io/projects/flyspace/): Visual data workspace. A visual workspace where you connect data sources to AI assistants and see which sources feed each answer. AI answers require running FLYSPACE locally with your own model, for example through Ollama. Formerly OmniOS.
  - Status: Live preview
  - Reflects: SyberLabs/Flyspace@e95ae73 · verified 2026-10-05
  - Source: https://github.com/SyberLabs/Flyspace
  - Live: https://omni.syberlabs.io/ (The preview opens as OmniOS. Your canvas stays in your browser.)
  - Evidence, deployed: The limited public preview has run at omni.syberlabs.io since 2026-10-03, deployed by hand from a recorded commit on Cloudflare Workers.
  - Evidence, tested: Unit tests across the stores, services and capability engine, and six Playwright specs including the “morning” golden path: shell → question → cited sources → crystal → second persona.
  - Evidence, implemented: The capability compiler and the server-side broker are implemented and hardened against fixtures and stubbed transports.
  - Evidence, not yet: No third-party API or MCP server has been measured in production use. Speech is tested with typed transcripts; there is no live microphone measurement. The hosted identity boundary exists in code with no provisioned issuer.

## Products



## Company

- [Consulting and partnerships](https://syberlabs.io/services/): Custom AI consulting, builds and design partnerships from SyberLabs. We design agent systems that check their own work: host-run checks, signed records and human approval before anything ships.
- [Research](https://syberlabs.io/research/): Every SyberLabs research artifact on one page: the technical reports and notes on this site, the RISE reader-owned AI status pages, the five working papers in SyberLabs/papers, the Instrument Panel and the OSAHR decision workbench. Each card states the claim, the evidence state it has reached, what it does not establish, the date and the source.

## Account

- [Subscriber account](https://rise.syberlabs.io/plus/): Existing RISE subscribers
- [Privacy](https://syberlabs.io/privacy/): What syberlabs.io does with visitor data: a static site with no accounts, forms, cookies or analytics for visitors, and an invite-only staff sign-in.

## Design system

- [Atlas kit v2](https://syberlabs.io/kit/v2/): SyberLabs Design System v2 "Atlas" kit. Files: `syber-atlas.css` (tokens + components), `syber-atmosphere.js` (Plate I engine), `syber-sigil.js` (product sigils), `syber-mark-96.png`, `demo.html`.
- [Kit README](https://syberlabs.io/kit/v2/README.md): Sections: Current website direction: immersive mathematical media, Vendoring, CSS, JS (ES modules, no dependencies), Rules (accessibility and performance).

## How we build

- [The factory](https://syberlabs.io/factory/): Inside SyberLabs' autonomous software factory: agents propose code as Git candidates, the host runs every check on the exact tree, ordered rules and a person admit each change, and every step is a signed record.
- [/approach/](https://syberlabs.io/approach/): How SyberLabs builds AI software: establish what a system knows, design what a person can do with it, and verify that they can review and change the result.
- [/stack/](https://syberlabs.io/stack/): How SyberLabs’ coding agents read open-source dependencies at the exact version a project uses, through GitHits, and what that sends off our machines.
